page: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is a General Purpose virtual server belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features 16 shared vCPUs mapped from 8 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a local 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and there are no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results place this server consistently in the average tier for most multi-core and memory operations. The multi-core stress-ng score reaches 21535.52, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 6565.0. Single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with a Geekbench single-core score of 836.0 and text processing of 593.0, both falling into the poor category. However, memory bandwidth remains solid, with read-only small block cached speeds at 1518.77 GB/sec and large block uncached speeds at 107.12 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require high memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage without needing constant, dedicated single-core CPU performance. It is well-suited for static web serving, which benchmarked at 12.01 GB/sec, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. It can also handle lightweight machine learning tasks, such as small-model LLM inference, achieving 115.24 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model.
description: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is a General Purpose virtual server from the Cloud Compute family, configured with 16 shared vCPUs on an Intel Xeon x86_64 architecture with 8 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of RAM and a 1280 GB local NVMe SSD, with no integrated GPU. Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 21535.52 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6565.0. However, single-core performance is limited, as shown by a poor Geekbench single-core score of 836.0. The server delivers solid memory bandwidth, reaching 107.12 GB/sec for large block reads, and supports 23.04 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. This resource profile is suitable for static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded processing workloads that benefit from high memory and fast local storage capacity under a shared CPU model.
